title: Working With JSON Responses

content.intro: In this lesson, you will work through working with json responses with a focused jQuery example. The subtopics below preserve the supplied curriculum coverage and connect the API idea to a small browser interface.
content.why_it_matters: This topic is useful because it turns reading json objects into a repeatable implementation choice. AJAX sends HTTP requests without requiring a full-page navigation. Treat network errors, HTTP failures, CORS policy, authentication, timeouts, and malformed response data as distinct cases.

task_acceptance_criteria: The implementation demonstrates working with json responses using a current, documented approach.
The learner records the expected and actual behavior and checks at least one edge case.

The test setup and any runtime limitation are documented honestly.

common_mistakes: Assuming a selector matched an element without checking the collection length.
Confusing jQuery collections with native DOM elements or live properties with markup attributes.
Using .html() with untrusted data or assuming client-side validation enforces server rules.
Treating a demo snippet as production-ready without testing failure and accessibility states.
